title: The Folded Lane and the Lost Locket
markdown:
The lane behind St. Jude’s would not sit still. Leo adjusted his spectacles and called it the Folded Lane: known, and not. He had come to chart its quirks. Marmalade, ginger, who treated personal space as myth, batted his compass.

“Precision is key,” Leo said, moving the paw.

The world lurched. Silver light. Heat-haze. A breath later the lane looked the same, but he had seen Chloe, his best friend, weeping into her hands over a lost locket.

The silver heart held a faded photo of her brother Liam, who had vanished months ago. It was what she had left of him. Mapping could wait.

Plan A: intercept the locket. He sketched vantage points. Marmalade streaked ahead. Chloe came along the lane, worried. Mr. Grumbles, church groundskeeper, emerged from the hall with his usual scowl.

“Lurking?” he boomed.

Leo fumbled the sketch onto the man’s boots. Plan A died. “Loitering. Trespassing.” Grumbles snatched the paper, eyed the compass. “Nonsense. Mischief. Be off.”

The map, Leo’s way of understanding the lane, went into a jacket. Stakes doubled. Chloe’s fingers found the empty place at her neck. “I had it when I came this way.”

Leo’s plans had a habit of collapsing. Marmalade never did. Chloe, distressed, still saw what other people walked past. “Did you hear anything? A jingle. A thud.”

She frowned. “At the old oak. Tiny bells. I thought it was wind.”

Marmalade stared at the roots and purred. Sunlight cut the leaves and found a crevice. Dust. A glint of silver.

“It slipped,” Leo said.

Too narrow for his hand. Marmalade nudged a stone into a ramp. Chloe reached, felt cool metal, drew the heart out. Relief arrived without speeches.

Leo looked at the oak, the crevice, Grumbles’s retreating scowl. Being chased had put them at the tree. Losing the map had made him look. Marmalade stretched, content, a cat who had been right in the loudest possible way, which this time was a purr.

Leo did not reach for a more elaborate plan. He watched Chloe fasten the locket and kept his eyes on the lane as it folded, slightly, like a page he no longer needed to flatten.
characters: Leo (careful boy cartographer who keeps making plans that are almost too clever), Marmalade (a cat with excellent instincts and terrible manners)
audience: teenagers aged 13-15, fantastic mystery adventure for young teens
author: StoryGen Community
